goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
goldens.reasoning: G1 flags side effects in the check method causing race conditions; C3 identifies the race condition in the stats update inside should_block?. C1 discusses the same side effect but a different consequence (rollback), so not counted.

goldens.comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
goldens.reasoning: C2 explicitly identifies the case-sensitive lookup bypass.

candidates: app/models/blocked_email.rb:11 - Match statistics are rolled back whenever the block actually happens.. `should_block?` runs inside `User#valid?`, and ActiveRecord runs that inside the transaction that `user.save` opens. When the email is blocked, validation fails, `save` returns false and the transaction is rolled back. That rollback also undoes the `match_count`/`last_match_at` update made here. So for `:block` records, the counters never change during real signups. They only move for `:do_nothing` records or when `should_block?` is called on its own, as the spec does. Record the match outside the user's transaction (for example in a separate connection or job, or after the failed save in the controller), or move the check out of the model validation. I couldn't see whether `UsersController#create` uses `user.save`, but that is the usual path.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 - Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so changing letter case gets past the block.. `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up as `Bad@Spammers.org` is not matched, so the block is trivially bypassed. Nothing shown here downcases the email before validation. Normalize both sides: store the email lowercased and look it up with `where(email: email.downcase)` (or `lower(email)`). Ideally make the unique index case-insensitive as well.

app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 - Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses increments under concurrency.. The count is loaded, incremented in Ruby and saved back. Two signups that check the same email at once both read N and write N+1, so a match is lost. Do the increment in the database instead, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.
